# Business plan

> What we sell and to whom, what has to be true for it to work, the first 90 days and the risks.
>
> This is the starting draft that ships with the back end, as it was written. The copy people work from is in the back end, under [Plans](https://quickpickle.vercel.app/backstage/plans/docs/business-plan), and may have been changed there since. This file does not follow those changes.

**What this is:** the working plan for Quick Pickle on a few pages. It is a draft to argue with, not a finished document. Anything marked _Assumption_ has not been checked yet.

_Starter draft, written from what was known on 12 November 2026. Rewrite it as you learn. Every save is kept in the history, so nothing is lost by changing it._

## What we sell

Quick Pickle is pickle juice in a shot. The juice is clear and there are no pickles in the bottle. It comes in a 100 ml clear plastic bottle with a white screw cap.

We sell it direct, online, to addresses in New Zealand. Every price and cost in this plan is in New Zealand dollars.

Packs of 6, 12 and 24 are planned. Their names and prices on the site are stand-ins until you confirm them.

What we are really selling is four things, and only these four:

- **The taste.** Sour, salty, properly pickly. Everyone pulls the face.
- **The tiny bottle.** One twist, down in one. It lives in the kit bag.
- **The ritual.** Before the whistle, at the half, on the sideline with the oranges.
- **Lucky.** The superhero cat who comes with every shot.

## Who it is for

_Assumption._ People with a game-day ritual: club players, weekend runners, social-grade netballers, the parent running the sideline. They buy it because it tastes like something and is fun to hand round the team.

_Assumption._ The person who buys is often buying for more than themselves: a captain, a coach, a manager or a parent. That is who the 24 pack is for.

Nobody has tested either of these with real people yet. The [marketing plan](../plans/marketing-plan.md) says how to test them cheaply.

## How we sell it

- From our own site and our own checkout. No marketplace and no retailer to start with.
- Payments will go through Stripe, once there is an account in the business's name.
- A courier takes it to the door. The delivery prices on the site are stand-ins until a courier quotes.
- The site is built but not launched. Today the checkout is in test mode: it records an order and charges nobody.
- _Not decided:_ whether the first sale is a pre-order for a first batch, or stock on the shelf. The site is set up as a pre-order for now.

## What has to be true for this to work

A plan is a list of bets. These are ours. Each one stays an assumption until there is a number or an answer beside it.

1. **People like it enough to buy it twice.** A first order can be curiosity. A second order is the business. _How we will know:_ the [Customers](https://quickpickle.vercel.app/backstage/customers) screen shows how many orders each customer has placed.
2. **A pack leaves money after everything.** After the juice, bottle, cap, label, carton, courier and card fee, there is enough left on each pack to pay the monthly costs and to find the next customer. _How we will know:_ the [Budget](https://quickpickle.vercel.app/backstage/plans/budget), once real costs are in it. Today every cost there is a blank.
3. **We can make it safely, and the same every time.** A registered food plan, a label that has been checked, and a batch record for every production day. _How we will know:_ nothing under Making food or The label on the [compliance checklist](https://quickpickle.vercel.app/backstage/plans/compliance) is still waiting.
4. **We can sell it without saying what it does to a body.** _How we will know:_ people buy from a page that only talks about the taste, the bottle, the ritual and Lucky.
5. **We can reach buyers cheaply.** Clubs, teams, events, the Pickle Crew list and word of mouth, without paying for every sale with advertising. _How we will know:_ where each order came from, and what it cost to get.
6. **It arrives in one piece.** A plastic bottle of liquid has to survive a courier. _How we will know:_ send test parcels to yourself and to a rural address before the first real order, then count how many real orders arrive damaged.

## The first 90 days

_Assumption: the clock starts on the day the questions that hold up launch are answered. Nothing below has a date on purpose._

The step-by-step version is the [launch checklist](../plans/launch-checklist.md).

**Days 1 to 30: real answers and real numbers.**

- Answer the [questions that hold up launch](https://quickpickle.vercel.app/backstage/plans/questions).
- Find out which food plan applies, and register.
- Settle the recipe, the label wording and the date mark with whoever makes it.
- Get real quotes for juice, bottles, caps, labels, cartons and the courier. Put each one in the Budget.
- Set up the legal entity, the bank account, Stripe and the customer email address.
- Set prices once the Budget shows what a pack costs.

**Days 31 to 60: a small first batch and a quiet launch.**

- Make the first batch, with a complete batch record.
- Send test parcels. Fix the packaging if anything leaks.
- Open to the Pickle Crew list and to people you know first. Small enough that a mistake is cheap.
- Pack and send every order yourself from the packing sheet, and fix the sheet where it is wrong.
- Ask every early customer one thing: would you order again?

**Days 61 to 90: learn, then decide.**

- Look at the numbers below.
- Try one or two channels from the marketing plan properly, one at a time.
- Decide: make a second batch the same, change something first, or stop. Stopping after one small batch is a fine result if the numbers say so.

## The numbers that matter

Keep it to a handful.

| Number                                               | Where it lives                |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| What is left on each pack after costs                | Budget                        |
| Packs a month needed to cover the monthly costs      | Budget, under Break-even      |
| Orders, and money in                                 | Orders                        |
| Customers who have ordered more than once            | Customers                     |
| People on the Pickle Crew list                       | Today                         |
| Orders that went wrong: damaged, missing, complaints | Notes on the order, and Tasks |

Accounting is not done here. Sales, costs and tax are for Xero and your accountant. The Budget is for setting prices and seeing whether a pack pays for itself. It is not the books.

## Risks

**The big one: in New Zealand a food cannot be sold on what it does to a body.** That covers the label, the site, emails, captions, replies to customers and anything a stockist says for us. _Assumption, from a desk look at other brands' websites and not checked by us:_ other pickle juice brands lean on exactly those claims. We do not, and cannot. So the brand sells the taste, the tiny bottle, the ritual and Lucky. Every word that goes out is checked against the copy rules, and there is a sheet for the day a customer asks: [How to answer a health question](../how-to/how-to-answer-a-health-question.md). The short name for this rule is "no health claims".

The others, in the order they are likely to bite:

- **Food safety.** One bad batch can end a small food business. The answer is boring: a registered plan, a batch record every time, and a recall sheet you have read before you need it.
- **The label.** A label that misses something means a reprint, or worse. Have it checked before printing a large run.
- **The sums.** Small bottles of liquid are heavy for their price, and couriers usually charge by size and weight. Delivery may eat what is left on the small packs. The Budget will show it once the courier's quote is in.
- **Leaks and breakages in the post.** Test parcels first.
- **One person.** If you are away, nothing ships. The how-to sheets exist so someone else can pack an order or run a production day from the page.
- **Supply.** One supplier for bottles or juice means one thing going wrong stops everything. Know the lead time and the second choice.
- **Shelf life.** _Not known yet._ Until it is, do not make more than you can sell well inside it.
- **The name and the cat.** Check that the name is free to use, and decide whether to register it and Lucky as trade marks.

## What is not decided yet

The open questions are on the [Questions](https://quickpickle.vercel.app/backstage/plans/questions) screen. The ones marked as holding up launch have to be answered before the site can take money. The big groups are the product facts (recipe, label, shelf life, where it is made), the offer (packs, prices, delivery), the business itself (legal entity, GST, bank, Stripe) and the claim lines from the concept deck.
